title: Bhature
description: Bhature is a soft, fluffy, deep-fried North Indian bread made from a lightly fermented dough. It is traditionally served with chole and is known for its airy texture, crisp golden exterior, and rich flavor.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: Warm water – as needed (about ½ cup)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Mix the Dry Ingredients
steps: In a large bowl, sift together the all-purpose flour, semolina, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Add Yogurt and Oil
steps: Add the yogurt and oil to the dry ingredients.
Mix until the mixture becomes crumbly.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Knead the Dough
steps: Gradually add warm water and knead into a smooth, soft, slightly sticky dough.
The dough should be softer than regular chapati dough.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Rest the Dough
steps: Cover the dough with a damp cloth.
Rest for at least 2 hours at room temperature to allow light fermentation.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Divide and Roll
steps: Knead the dough briefly after resting.
Roll each ball into a round disc about 5–6 inches in diameter using minimal flour.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Heat the Oil
steps: Heat enough oil for deep frying over medium-high heat.
The oil is ready when a small piece of dough rises immediately to the surface.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Fry the Bhature
steps: Carefully slide one rolled bhatura into the hot oil.
Press gently with a slotted spoon to help it puff up.
Flip and fry until both sides are golden brown.

instruction.title: Step 8 – Drain and Serve
steps: Remove the bhature using a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chole or your favorite curry.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Accompany with sliced onions, green chilies, lemon wedges, and mango pickle.
Pair with chilled lassi for a traditional North Indian meal.

chefTips: Resting the dough is essential for soft, fluffy bhature.
Use fresh yogurt to promote gentle fermentation.
Maintain a consistent oil temperature to achieve even puffing and prevent excess oil absorption.
Press gently with a slotted spoon while frying to encourage the bhature to puff completely.
